title: MCP Resources and Prompts — Context Exposure Beyond Tools

questions.question: What does handle_resources_list expose in addition to the five note resources?
questions.explanation: The list contains note-1 through note-5 plus notes://recent, which is the dynamic application/json resource.

questions.question: What does resources_read return for notes://recent?
options: A 404 because recent is not a note
questions.explanation: The dynamic URI is intentionally readable and returns a JSON list limited to the five latest notes.

questions.question: What notification follows an update to subscribed note-1?
questions.explanation: update_note checks subscribed URIs and emits a resources/updated notification for the changed note URI.

questions.question: What happens when prompts_get requests review_note with style concise?
options: The style is ignored and the prompt is rejected
It returns the summarize_tag prompt instead
It creates a new resource subscription
review_note uses note_id and concise style
questions.explanation: review_note accepts note_id plus optional style; the provided style is included in the generated user instruction.

questions.question: Which argument is required by the summarize_tag prompt?
questions.explanation: prompts_get defines summarize_tag with required tag, then returns an instruction to summarize notes carrying that tag.

questions.question: What is the practical distinction between a resource and a prompt in this lesson?
options: A resource can only be written; a prompt can only be binary
a resource supplies data; a prompt supplies a reusable message
A prompt always contains the full note database
questions.explanation: Resources expose context such as note content, while prompts package instructions and arguments for a model conversation.
